newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PENPIX OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN WOMEN'S SEMIFINALISTS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PENPIX OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN WOMEN'S SEMIFINALISTS.

text.p: Portraits of the women's semifinalists at the Australian Open:
Martina Hingis (Switzerland) v Mary Joe Fernandez (U.S.)

The most exciting prospect in women's tennis since Monica Seles. She has hardly put a foot wrong in Melbourne and hasn't dropped a set in five matches. Widely tipped to succeed Graf as number one and on present form could fulfil that expectation within the next two years. If she wins in Melbourne, Hingis will be the youngest grand slam champion of the professional era.
Seeding: 4. Age: 16. Plays: right-handed. Weight: 52kg. Height: 1.67m. Ranking: 4. Tournament wins: 3. Head-to-head (win-loss): 1-0. Career prize money: US$1.6 million.

Playing her best tennis in four years since reaching the final of the French Open. A true fighter, she has twice recovered from a set down. Fernandez, born in the Dominican Republic, reached career-high ranking of four in 1990 and 1991. She reached the final in Melbourne in 1990 and 1992.
Seeding: 14. Age: 25. Plays: right-handed. Weight: 63kg. Height: 1.77m. Ranking: 17. Tournament wins: 6. Head-to-head: 0-1. Career prize money: $4.2 million.
Amanda Coetzer (South Africa) v Mary Pierce (France)

Tournament giant-killer who disposed of world number one Steffi Graf in straight sets in the fourth round. Her groundstrokes, particularly the forehand, are lethal and she has the knack of the finding the lines. She is one of the smallest players on the women's tour, but has a strong serve. This is only her second grand slam semifinal after reaching the same stage of this tournament last year.
Seeding: 12. Age: 25. Plays: right-handed. Weight: 55kg. Height: 1.57m. Ranking: 14. Tournament wins: 3. Head-to-head: 1-1. Career prize money: $1.9 million.

Tournament diva who wears her heart on her sleeve, former champion Pierce has shown new mental strength in past weeks. She is still a crowd favourite in Melbourne after her 1995 victory -- fans love her aggressive, athletic game -- but will need all the support she can muster to defeat the tenacious South African. Pierce was born in Canada, plays for France and is based in the United States.
Seeding: unseeded. Age: 22. Plays: right-handed. Weight: 61 kg. Height: 1.80m. Ranking: 22. Tournament wins: 7. Head-to-head: 1-1. Career prize money: $2.3 million.
